sentences.text: Cretornis hlavaci was a pterosaur with a wingspan estimated between 1.5 and 1.6 meters, based on comparisons with relatives. Its humerus, the upper arm bone, measures approximately 3 inches in length.
A unique derived trait of this animal is that the distal part of its humerus has a diamond-shaped cross-section.
The known fossil material consists of a partial skeleton lacking a skull, including a complete humerus, ulna, radius, wrist, and two wing finger phalanges.
Fossils of Cretornis were discovered in 1880 by quarry workers in Zářecká Lhota, Czech Republic, who were extracting gravel for road repair.
A local resident named Mrs. Tomková alerted pharmacist and collector František Hlaváč to the fossil discovery.
Professor Antonín Frič originally identified the fossils in 1881 as a toothed bird the size of a swan and named the species Cretornis hlavaci.
The specific name 'hlavaci' honors the collector František Hlaváč.
Scientists later realized that the fossils originally identified as a bird actually belonged to a pterosaur.
The holotype fossils of Cretornis are currently housed in the National Museum in Prague.
In the nineteenth century, Cretornis was classified as a species within the genus Ornithocheirus.
A 2018 analysis by Nicholas Longrich and colleagues placed Cretornis within the family Nyctosauridae, a position that contradicts its placement within Azhdarchoidea.
Cretornis lived approximately 92 million years ago during the Turonian stage of the Late Cretaceous in what is now the Czech Republic.
The time range for Cretornis is estimated from 93.9 to 89.8 million years ago.
